# sysrst_ctrl Key-Triggered Interrupt Module Specification

## Overview

This module implements the key/input-triggered interrupt feature for the system reset controller. It monitors a set of system input conditions, detects stable edge transitions on those inputs, and reports each valid transition as an interrupt status event and as a consolidated interrupt pulse.

The module does not perform keyboard combo detection, output override, or EC reset pulse generation. It is limited to edge detection, debounce qualification, status reporting, and interrupt generation.

## Inputs Monitored

The module shall monitor the following six input channels:

- Power button
- Key 0
- Key 1
- Key 2
- AC present
- EC reset

The module operates on the logical levels presented to it. Any optional input polarity inversion is performed outside this module and is not part of its behavior. The module interprets only the levels it receives and the transitions between those levels.

## Configuration

The module receives configuration information that controls which transitions shall generate events:

- For each of the six input channels, enablement of low-to-high edge detection shall be independently programmable.
- For each of the six input channels, enablement of high-to-low edge detection shall be independently programmable.
- A common debounce interval shall apply to all channels and to both edge directions.

The configuration is assumed to be stable for normal operation. The module shall respond to the currently programmed enable settings and debounce interval.

## Edge Detection and Debounce Behavior

A valid low-to-high event shall be generated only when:

1. Low-to-high detection is enabled for that channel.
2. The input transitions from low to high.
3. The input remains high for the full programmed debounce interval.

A valid high-to-low event shall be generated only when:

1. High-to-low detection is enabled for that channel.
2. The input transitions from high to low.
3. The input remains low for the full programmed debounce interval.

The module shall not generate an event for a level condition alone. A transition must occur, and the new level must be maintained long enough to satisfy the debounce requirement.

If the input returns to its previous level before the debounce interval expires, no event shall be generated.

When the debounce condition is first satisfied, one event shall be generated. Holding the input at the same level shall not generate repeated events. After a valid event is generated, the module shall be able to detect a subsequent opposite-direction transition on the same channel.

Each channel shall operate independently. Events on one channel shall not affect the detection behavior of another channel.

## Status Reporting

The module shall report events through a status interface that contains one indicator for each combination of input channel and edge direction. This is a total of twelve event indicators:

- Power button low-to-high
- Power button high-to-low
- Key 0 low-to-high
- Key 0 high-to-low
- Key 1 low-to-high
- Key 1 high-to-low
- Key 2 low-to-high
- Key 2 high-to-low
- AC present low-to-high
- AC present high-to-low
- EC reset low-to-high
- EC reset high-to-low

When a valid event is detected, the module shall drive the corresponding status update output so that the associated status bit is set to 1.

The module shall not generate a status update for a disabled edge direction, for an unstable input, or when no transition has occurred.

If multiple valid events occur in the same clock cycle, the module shall report all of them simultaneously.

## Interrupt Output

The module shall provide a single consolidated interrupt output.

The interrupt output shall be asserted for one clock cycle when any valid event is detected in that cycle. If multiple events occur in the same cycle, the interrupt output shall still be asserted for one clock cycle. If no event occurs, the interrupt output shall not be asserted.

The interrupt output shall not be asserted for:

- Disabled edge directions.
- Input changes that do not meet the debounce requirement.
- A static input level, even if it is the same as a recently detected edge target level.

## Reset Behavior

When the module is reset:

- All internal event detection state shall be cleared.
- No status update pulses shall be generated.
- The interrupt output shall be deasserted.

A transition that occurred before reset shall not be reported after reset. Simply being at a particular input level after reset shall not be treated as an event; an enabled debounced transition must occur after reset to generate a status update or interrupt.

## Scope and Non-Requirements

The module shall only generate event indications. It shall not:

- Clear or write zero into any interrupt status bit.
- Generate repeated events while an input remains at a stable level.
- Perform keyboard combo detection.
- Override any output pin.
- Generate EC reset or system reset actions.
- Lock or modify configuration registers.

The behavior of this module is limited to qualifying input transitions, reporting valid transitions as status events, and producing a consolidated interrupt indication.
